summary: Ruth W. Dunnell works in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987-1988), and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

Ryan Anningson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and completed his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, D. Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, and three traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (AB, 2001) and Harvard University (PhD, 2010), later holding posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013-2015), and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryōshō Taira (1906-1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Taisho University, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 1976 and further attested in 1984.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015-2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909-2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937-1940), under Shun'ichi Takagi, Ryťjō Yamada, and Ryotai Hatani. He lectured at Berlin and served as professor at Ryukoku (attested 1963-1974).
Ryoichi Kondo (1930-2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojun Mitomo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Ryokei Kaginushi (1926-2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Nobuyoshi Yamabe. He served as a professor at Otani University, including in the Faculty of Letters (attested 1978, 1987-1993).

Ryoko Mochizuki (1933-) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo until 1963, Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972 and 1983).

Ryomin Akizuki (1921-1999) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947-1950) and taught Makio Takemura. He held a post at Saitama Medical University (~1973-1991).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872-1946) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Atsuuji Ashikaga. Educated at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1892-1895), he held posts at Ryukoku, the Third Higher School, and Kyoto University.

Ryosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at Dongguk University (1986). Posts included lecturer at Daegu University (1988), researcher at the Institute for Religious Culture, and professorial appointments at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Ryukoku University (attested 2011-2013).

Ryosei Fukuda (1937-2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and taught Ryuichi Abe. He served as professor (1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012), and led several Buddhist institutes.

Ryoshin Nakao (1952-) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Komazawa University (~1971-1980), Nakao worked at the Research Institute of Soto Studies (~1980-1990) and became a professor at Hanazono University (~1996).

Ryosho Hayashi (1927-2008) studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, focusing on Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served at Taisho University as professor (1975), Dean of Letters (1981), and professor emeritus (1990-1994), and headed the Japan-Korea Cultural Exchange Association (1990).

Ryosho Nakamura (1927-2013) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura (~1949-1953), and Rissho University (DLitt, 1977), later serving as professor at The International University of Kagoshima (~1968-1998).
Ryosho Onami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. Onami served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).

Ryoshu Koda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koda held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).
